review_notes: I read all 42 lines of PinnedSigns.lean. I also read the definitions it depends on: signFieldEquiv, its simp lemmas and compatibleSigns in BondSigns.lean, bondSubspace in BondSubspace.lean, and pinnedBondSubspace in BondPin.lean. I checked how the file's declarations are used later, in SignedSigns.lean (prescribedCompatibleSignsEquiv, prescribedCompatibleSigns_card_of_nonempty) and in PinnedBonds.lean. There are two findings. First, the new set `positiveCompatibleSigns` has no membership lemma, so the proof in this file and the one later use both unfold it with `change`. Second, the simp proof gets from `signFieldEquiv (s v) = 0` to `s v = true` by applying the existing simp lemma `signFieldEquiv_true` backwards. That only works around a missing canonical lemma, and the call also lists `Equiv.apply_eq_iff_eq` twice. Some uncertainty remains. The `change` at SignedSigns.lean:61 also unfolds `prescribedCompatibleSigns` and `signTranslate`, so the membership lemma would remove only part of that work. The proposed lemmas are untested; both should hold by `Iff.rfl` or a case split on Bool. The `signFieldEquiv` lemma belongs in BondSigns.lean, so it is anchored at the line in this file where the workaround appears. I did not count the theorems `positiveCompatibleSigns_card` and `positiveCompatibleSigns_sum` as missing simp lemmas: they are cardinality and counting identities used by explicit `exact`/`rw`, and are not normal-form rewrites.

findings.excerpt:
def positiveCompatibleSigns (left right : E → V) (B : Set V) (η : E → Bool) : Set (V → Bool) :=
  {s | s∈compatibleSigns left right η ∧ ∀ v∈B,s v=true}
findings.problem: This new set-valued definition has no membership lemma. `simp` cannot see through `s ∈ positiveCompatibleSigns left right B η`, so every consumer has to unfold the definition by hand with `change`. That happens in this file, in positiveCompatibleSignsEquiv (lines 20–22: `change ((∀ e,η e=true → s (left e)=s (right e)) ∧ ∀ v∈B,s v=true) ↔ ...`). It happens again in SignedSigns.lean, prescribedCompatibleSignsEquiv (`change (s∈compatibleSigns left right η ∧ ∀ v∈B,s v=true) ↔ ...`). Each of these restates the definition's body verbatim, which is brittle if the definition changes.
findings.proposed_change:
Add the standard membership lemma right after the definition:

@[simp] theorem mem_positiveCompatibleSigns {left right : E → V} {B : Set V} {η : E → Bool} {s : V → Bool} :
    s ∈ positiveCompatibleSigns left right B η ↔ s ∈ compatibleSigns left right η ∧ ∀ v ∈ B, s v = true := Iff.rfl

Then use `simp only [mem_positiveCompatibleSigns, ...]` or `rw [mem_positiveCompatibleSigns]` in place of restating the body with `change`, both here and in prescribedCompatibleSignsEquiv. A similar `mem_compatibleSigns` lemma would let simp go one step further when needed.
findings.benefit: Users get one canonical simp-normal form for membership. Proofs no longer copy the definition's body into `change` goals, and `simp` can work with hypotheses such as `hs : s ∈ positiveCompatibleSigns ...` without manual unfolding. The definition can also change without silently breaking every `change` that restates it.

findings.problem: The pinned condition reaches the form `signFieldEquiv (s v) = 0`, and the goal wants `s v = true`. The existing simp set has no rule for this: `signFieldEquiv_true` only rewrites the closed term `signFieldEquiv true` to `0`. The proof therefore uses the simp lemma backwards (`← signFieldEquiv_true`). Inside this call, that rewrites every `(0 : SignField)` into `signFieldEquiv true` so that `Equiv.apply_eq_iff_eq` can fire, and `Equiv.apply_eq_iff_eq` is listed twice to make the ordering work. Using a simp lemma against its orientation is a workaround for a missing canonical lemma. It also cannot be reused: a plain `simp` here would rewrite `signFieldEquiv true` straight back to `0`, so the two lemmas fight, and the trick only works inside a hand-picked `simp only` list.
findings.proposed_change:
Next to `signFieldEquiv_true`/`signFieldEquiv_false` in BondSigns.lean, add the iff forms that are the right normal form for equations with a variable argument, for example:

@[simp] theorem signFieldEquiv_eq_zero_iff {b : Bool} : signFieldEquiv b = 0 ↔ b = true := by cases b <;> decide
@[simp] theorem signFieldEquiv_eq_one_iff {b : Bool} : signFieldEquiv b = 1 ↔ b = false := by cases b <;> decide

(adjust the proof tactic as needed). Then change the call here to `simp only [Equiv.apply_eq_iff_eq, funext_iff, Pi.zero_apply, Subtype.forall, signFieldEquiv_eq_zero_iff]`, which drops both the `←` and the duplicated entry.
findings.benefit: `signFieldEquiv b = 0` gets a forward-oriented normal form that agrees with the existing simp lemmas instead of competing with them. The proof becomes a plain forward simp call that does not depend on rewriting every `0` in the goal. Later developments that pin signs to `true` (or to `false`, via the `= 1` form) can use the same lemma.
